method: First reasoned review of the supplied bytes using atomscan, cleave facts, rizin control-flow disassembly, pefile, and token-resolved dnfile/dncil IL. Static analysis only; no sample was executed. Reputation and filenames were not used as behavioral proof.

samples.identification: StormAttack/Shtormec-style x86 persistence and DLL-injection loader with erased resources
evidence: Entry 0x402674 reaches dispatcher 0x401cb0. The configuration DWORD at file 0x4120 is 3; the 0x401f75 branch calls Active Setup installer 0x401900 and self-delete helper 0x401390.

0x401900 constructs a GUID-named HKLM Active Setup Installed Components key, sets expandable StubPath at 0x401a4b, reads and patches its own image via CRT file I/O, writes the copy with fwrite, and starts the copied path using CreateProcessA.
0x401390 reads its module path, converts it to a short pathname, reads COMSPEC, constructs /c del plus the self path and > nul, then creates/resumes the cleanup process.

Alternate modes retain extraction of DLL resource 101, LanmanServer Parameters/ServiceDLL replacement, and 0x401150 remote DLL injection: CreateProcessA, VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, Kernel32!LoadLibraryA resolution, and CreateRemoteThread with that export and remote pathname.
samples.limits: The .rsrc directory and contents are entirely zero-filled; no DLL can be recovered from this copy. These are retained code capabilities, not proof of successful installation or injection. No evidence supports the collector filename’s WannaCry/ransomware attribution.

samples.identification: ExtremeRansomwareBotnet managed ransomware/keylogger implant (internal program identity)
evidence: Main (method 0x0600001a) hides its ProgramData work directory, locks the workstation, shows an extortion form, blocks input, invokes Defender/service disabling and fodhelper hijacking, installs persistence, and starts surveillance tasks.

StartKeylogger installs low-level keyboard hook 13; HookCallback checks WM_KEYDOWN, reads the key code through Marshal.ReadInt32, appends timestamped key names to KEYLOG_FILE, and calls CallNextHookEx. A separate delegate polls GetAsyncKeyState and records characters.
ContinuousScreenshot copies the primary screen into a Bitmap, saves timestamped JPEGs, and repeats after 30000 ms. ClipboardMonitor records clipboard text.

ContinuousDataExfiltration reads keys.log and clip.log, bounds their transmitted tails, wraps them as keylog/clipboard payload objects, and calls SendToC2. Its async state machine serializes JSON into FormUrlEncodedContent and calls HttpClient.PostAsync using the C2_URL field initialized to http://artacle.io.

ReadBrowserData constructs the Chrome Default profile path and copies Cookies, History, and Login Data into the Stolen directory. SafeBoot registry trees and shadow copies are deletion targets. Run-key and logon-task commands use the self-image path.
RealEncryption enumerates Desktop/TestFolder recursively, reads each file, calls EncryptAES, writes a suffixed output, then deletes the input. CreateRansomNotes and the lock form demand payment.
samples.limits: AES_KEY is the 17-byte UTF-8 HiddenTearsKey123 value and AES_IV is 15 bytes. set_Key throws before the output/delete path; errors are caught. Encryption is attempted, not successful. Self-labels blackcat and HiddenTears do not prove those recognized families. Some added methods are ineffective; no DDoS or successful PDF exploitation is inferred from method names.

samples.identification: Modified static x86-64 Mirai-lineage IoT bot
evidence: ELF entry 0x400194 passes main 0x405230 to libc startup. Main initializes the hidden string table, detaches, registers attack-vector function pointers (0x400740), starts the Telnet scanner (0x406690), connects a controller socket, and receives length-framed tasks.

The received body at 0x405b85 is passed directly to 0x400410 at 0x405ba1. This parser reads network-order duration, vector, target count, IPv4/CIDR records and option records, then calls attack dispatch 0x4001c0 at 0x400633. The dispatch forks and invokes the vector-selected function pointer. This path remains intact independently of any flood send mutation.

0x406690 forks a scanner, creates an AF_INET/SOCK_RAW/IPPROTO_TCP socket, builds TCP SYN packets with destination port 23 at 0x40680e, and installs weighted default-credential pairs. 0x4064d0 copies and XOR-decodes each username/password with byte 0x22; scanner states send credentials and shell commands after Telnet prompt processing.

String table lock/unlock loops at 0x408410 and 0x408490 XOR four byte lanes of each of eight key words into bounded buffers. Their effective combined byte key is 0x51. Decoded strings include procfs paths, shell dialogue, daemon command lines, a Source Engine query, and a temporary-directory cleanup command.
samples.limits: The selected UDP vector loop at file 0x3359 calls the ret at 0x40b487 rather than send wrapper 0x40b488 (call file offset 0x336c). The old combined remote-UDP-flood rule correctly stays absent. Other vector routines retain send calls; this one mutation does not disable the entire bot.
trait_changes: Factor receive-to-parser evidence from the old combined UDP rule into a command-and-control observation, preserving relative-call target bindings and text-section/architecture scope. Pair it with hidden IoT credentials for the hostile bot finding.

Move the independent UDP socket/repeated-send observation into neutral communications/flood at notable severity. The original composite still requires both task reception and a call bound to the send syscall wrapper.
Detect the eight-word, four-lane XOR table loop under direction-neutral data/encoding/xor, at notable severity.

Require device-specific credential evidence in the stripped Mirai identity rule. Remove the generic backdoor-daemons-ref identity alias and use the existing neutral remote-daemon-name-cluster observation. Change the credential-required identity mapping from shell execution to T1110.001.

controls: check.py passed nine static mutation controls: supplied redirected send, restored send, redirected parser handoff, redirected body receive, removed credentials, removed XOR lanes, patterns outside .text, wrong architecture, and generic daemon/procfs paths without malicious code. No broad sample or package exception was added.
reference: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jgamblin/Mirai-Source-Code/master/mirai/bot/scanner.c (compared credential ordering and Telnet state machine after tracing the binary; source similarity is corroboration only)

verification.rescans: All three atomscan runs completed using CLEAVE_TRAITS_DIR=. --no-update --mode slow; all three were independently compared using cleave JSON. Native and managed findings are unchanged. ELF adds the independently bound command parser, hostile credential-bot composite, and notable direction-neutral XOR loop. The redirected UDP-loop finding remains absent.
